subsystems.name: Foundation model
subsystems.role: core reasoning engine: understands instructions, generates plans and text.

subsystems.name: Planner
subsystems.role: breaks a high-level goal into ordered, actionable steps.

subsystems.name: Memory
subsystems.role: retains project state, past actions and learned facts across long tasks.

subsystems.name: Tool interface
subsystems.role: lets the agent act beyond text — call APIs, run code, search the web.

subsystems.name: Verifier
subsystems.role: checks each output against goals or tests and triggers correction.

subsystems.name: Orchestrator
subsystems.role: runs the plan-act-observe-verify loop and manages state.

buildSteps.title: Select or train the foundation model
buildSteps.detail: Choose a large language model with strong reasoning and instruction-following, or fine-tune one on examples of multi-step tasks.

buildSteps.title: Define the tool set
buildSteps.detail: List every external action the agent may take — reading files, calling APIs, running code — with strict input/output schemas.

buildSteps.title: Build the memory system
buildSteps.detail: Set up a vector database to store and retrieve past steps and facts; add summarisation to keep the active context within the model's window.

buildSteps.title: Implement planning
buildSteps.detail: Prompt the model to decompose goals into steps, or train a separate planner; represent steps as a dependency graph so order can adapt.

buildSteps.title: Create the execution loop
buildSteps.detail: Code the cycle: plan, act via tools, observe results, verify, then revise or continue. Add retries and hard limits to prevent runaway loops.

buildSteps.title: Add verification layers
buildSteps.detail: For code, run unit tests; for data, validate schemas; for open-ended work, use a second model as critic or require human approval at key checkpoints.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate on multi-step benchmarks
buildSteps.detail: Assemble realistic project tasks, measure success rate, cost, and failure modes, then iterate on prompts, memory design and tool reliability.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Run tools in sandboxes with least-privilege permissions, rate-limit actions, log every step, and keep rollback and human override available.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with strong reasoning
prerequisites.why: they provide the core ability to understand instructions and generate plausible plans.
they let the model invoke external actions in a structured, reliable way.
they enable memory beyond the model's context window.
they safely contain generated code and other risky actions.
unit tests work for code, but checking a legal brief or a marketing plan is much harder.
current models still drift, repeat steps or lose the goal over many actions.

pathway.milestone: single-task agents (coding assistants, customer-service bots) that handle narrow, well-defined jobs with human oversight
multi-step agents that complete projects in domains with clear success criteria, such as coding and data analysis, with minimal supervision
agents that manage ambiguous knowledge work using learned verification and memory, with human review at checkpoints
teams of specialised agents that collaborate on large projects with robust verification and safety guarantees
